tools.name: fetch
tools.title: Fetch a record
tools.description: Read one full record (an answer, Action, prompt or page) by the citeladder:// id another read returned. Never construct an id.

id.description: A citeladder:// id exactly as a read returned it.

tools.name: get_project_business_context
tools.title: Get project overview
tools.description: Read one overview of a project in a single call: its identity and markets (with the market ids other tools take), then a short summary per section: business profile with owned domains and tracked competitors, latest visibility, the top 10 Actions, active prompts, Site Health, AI crawler access, demand, search performance, AI referrals, crawler logs, connected data and keyword research. Use it first to orient yourself, then the matching read_* tool for depth or paging (each section is that tool's default read). Omit sections for all of them; pass a few to keep the response small. A section can be unavailable on its own, such as visibility with no completed run (no_completed_run) or with the latest run's results still being written (metrics_pending, try again later).

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

sections.description: The sections to read; omit for all. profile also returns owned domains and competitors.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List the projects this connection can read. Start here when no project is known: every other project tool needs the id it returns. Each project has its id, name, brand, website, industry, primary market and the workspace it belongs to. Projects come oldest first, 50 per page by default; pass next_cursor for more. An empty list means no workspace was approved for this connection. To find a project by name use search; for one project in depth use get_project_business_context.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: open_analytics
tools.title: Open CiteLadder
tools.description: Show the user the CiteLadder project picker, in clients that display apps, so they can choose a project to view. Use list_projects to find projects yourself.

tools.name: read_actions
tools.title: Read Actions
tools.description: List the work CiteLadder recommends to improve visibility, highest priority first. Statuses: open (New), in_progress (accepted), done (declared implemented; its measurement is measuring or verified) and dismissed (Declined). By default it lists only open and in-progress Actions; pass status any to list every status, and query to find Actions whose title contains that text. Each item has its id, target (page, prompt or source), status, measurement, priority score, approach and link, and status_counts counts every status. Items come in pages; pass next_cursor for more. Pass site_url_id for the Actions on one page, or group_by for the grouped tree (the count and top items per group). Pass action_id for one Action in full: its diagnosis, each finding with its remediation, the measured outcome and any declaration.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

action_id.description: An Action id from a previous list, to read that one Action in full.

status.description: Keep only Actions with this status; any keeps every status. Omitted: open and in progress only.

query.description: Keep only Actions whose title contains this text (case-insensitive). Combine with status any to search every status.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_ai_ads
tools.title: Read ads in AI answers
tools.description: Paid ads shown in ChatGPT Search answers for the latest or a chosen run: ad presence rate ("N of M ChatGPT answers"), advertisers with share and first/last seen, the ad share and best rank of the brand itself, text creatives (paged) and prompts that surface ads with competitor ads beside organic brand mentions. Only ChatGPT Search shows ads; other engines are not_applicable, never zero. Ads are paid placements: report them separately, never as citations, sources or a cause of visibility.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_ai_crawlability
tools.title: Read AI crawler access
tools.description: Read whether the site's robots.txt lets each AI crawler in, for the latest or a chosen crawl: whether robots.txt was fetched (and its status), the sitemaps it lists, and per crawler (such as GPTBot or ClaudeBot) its operator, purpose, the matching rule, root access and how many sampled URLs it may not fetch. This is permission, not observed visits: use read_crawl_logs for crawlers that actually came. unavailable no_site_crawl means no crawl exists; robots_not_observed means the crawl could not read robots.txt. view history lists robots.txt as each crawl saw it, newest first.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

crawl_id.description: A crawl id that read_site_health returned; omit for the latest crawl.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_ai_referrals
tools.title: Read AI referral traffic
tools.description: Visits that arrived from AI assistants such as ChatGPT, from GA4: sessions, share of all traffic, key events and top landing pages for a range. These are people clicking through; read_crawl_logs has crawler requests. An unavailable state means no referral data has been imported, which is not zero; read_integration_status says why.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

range.description: A preset window ending today; or pass start_date and end_date instead.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

tools.name: read_ai_shelf
tools.title: Read the AI Shelf
tools.description: Read how AI answers recommend products for an ecommerce project, per product over a window of days. Without holder_id it returns the categories with product counts and one page of products, most visible first: for each, its holder_id, kind (owned, approved_competitor or ai_observed_competitor), visibility (share of the answers in scope that named it), appearances, win rate (share of its ordered appearances at rank 1), mean position, the median mentioned price beside the catalog price, and the merchant domains answers send shoppers to; executions is the number of answers in scope. source all adds competitors to your catalog; category_id narrows to one category; pass next_cursor for more. With holder_id it returns that product's page: the same metrics, its description and image, the products competing in the same answers, merchants, cited sources, fan-out queries, per-prompt metrics, the answers it appeared in (won, lost or unranked, with rank) and its open Actions. A null metric is unavailable (no answer in scope, or no ordered appearance), never zero. view overview is the shopping totals: shelf slots, share of shelf per brand, most and least visible products, merchants and fan-out. unavailable no_product_catalog means the project has no product catalog, which is normal for non-ecommerce brands; use read_visibility_overview for brand mentions instead. view catalog lists your products with their ids; competitor_candidates, buyer_prompts and discoveries (competitor searches still running) list the commerce setup with ids, each paged.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

view.description: products is visibility per product (the default); overview is the totals; the others are setup.

holder_id.description: A holder_id from a previous product list, to read that product in full.

source.description: catalog (the default) lists your products; all adds approved and AI-observed competitors.

category_id.description: A category id from this tool, to list only its products.

window_days.description: Days of answers to read, one of 7, 30, 90; omit for 30.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_ai_traffic_insights
tools.title: Read AI traffic insights
tools.description: Read the patterns CiteLadder found by joining AI crawler, referral and citation data for one saved window: pages crawled but never visited from AI, pages getting AI referrals but not crawled recently, crawler errors on valuable pages, and key events concentrated on few pages. Each pattern has a short explanation, the numbers behind it and the pages involved, with coverage. These are co-occurrence, not cause. It reads the newest saved 30-day window by default; custom dates must match a saved window exactly. unavailable means no insight snapshot exists yet, and coverage.notice says why, such as GA4 not being connected. Use read_ai_traffic_pages for the per-page numbers.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

range.description: A preset window ending today; or pass start_date and end_date instead.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

tools.name: read_ai_traffic_pages
tools.title: Read AI traffic by page
tools.description: Rank the project's own pages by AI activity, to find which pages AI crawlers fetch, AI assistants send visitors to and AI answers cite. Each row is one page (URL, path, folder, resource class) with four measures, each carrying its own coverage: AI crawler requests (server logs), AI referral sessions and key events (GA4), citations in AI answers, and Site Health findings, plus its last crawl. The window defaults to the last 30d; rows come 10 per page (up to 100); pass next_cursor for more. observed_crawl_coverage says how complete the logs are, and a measure without a connected source is missing, not zero. unavailable not_connected means no crawl logs, no GA4 and no completed visibility run in the window. Use read_ai_traffic_url for one page's timeline, read_crawl_logs for crawler-level detail, read_ai_referrals for site-wide referral totals, and read_site_pages for crawl data such as titles and scores.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

range.description: A preset window ending today; or pass start_date and end_date instead.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

folder.description: A site path prefix such as /blog/ to read only pages under it.

resource_class.description: A resource_class a previous row returned, such as page, to read only that kind.

verification.description: Keep only crawler requests whose claimed identity was verified, could not be verified, or failed verification.

sort.description: Row order by one measure, highest first, or by URL; omit for the default. Filters (folder, resource_class, verification) apply first.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_ai_traffic_url
tools.title: Read AI traffic for a URL
tools.description: Read the timeline of AI activity on one page of the project site, after read_ai_traffic_pages names it: the page's four measures (crawler requests, referral sessions, citations, Site Health findings) with their coverage and 4xx/5xx errors, then each crawler's first and last visit and request count, each AI source's first referral and sessions, and each citation by date and run. The window defaults to the last 30d. Each timeline is capped, and provenance.bounded is true when a cap was hit. The URL must be on the project's own site. unavailable url_not_joinable means the path cannot be matched (for example a redacted path); unavailable not_connected means no crawl logs, no GA4 and no completed visibility run in the window; unavailable with no reason means no activity was recorded for that page in the window.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

url.description: A page URL on the project site, as read_ai_traffic_pages listed it.

range.description: A preset window ending today; or pass start_date and end_date instead.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

tools.name: read_competitors
tools.title: Read competitors
tools.description: Read the competitors. view list is the tracked roster (names, aliases, domains) and the brand's own domains. view focus is one tracked competitor against the brand over a run: how many answers named it, the sources cited where it was named, and the prompts where it was named instead of the brand; it defaults to the latest completed run and takes topic_id. Use read_visibility_overview for every brand's rates side by side.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

view.description: list is the roster (the default); focus needs name; suggestions are pending.

name.description: With view focus: a tracked competitor exactly as view list names it.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: With view focus: a run id (audit_id); omit for the latest.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

topic_id.description: A topic id from read_prompt_portfolio; keep only answers to prompts filed under it when their run was measured. unavailable topic_not_measured means the run asked no prompt in it.

tools.name: read_content_differentiation
tools.title: Read content comparisons
tools.description: Read how the competitor pages AI answers cite differ from your own page on the topics they win. Use it before rewriting a page to compete. It returns up to the 10 newest comparison reports, each with its query, the owned page compared, the features both have (parity), those only competitors have (gaps) and those only you have, each with the share of inspected pages showing it. A report with state insufficient_evidence had fewer than 3 readable competitor pages or no matching owned page. An empty list means no comparison was made yet; this tool never reads new pages. Use read_visibility_sources to find the competing pages first.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

tools.name: read_crawl_logs
tools.title: Read AI crawler visits
tools.description: Read the AI crawler requests your server logs recorded, to see which crawlers actually visited, what they fetched and what they got back. View summary (the default) gives totals: requests, pages, active crawlers, error share and a daily series by purpose. View crawlers gives one row per crawler with status codes and verification. View coverage says how complete each day of logs is. View requests lists individual requests. The window defaults to the last 30d, except that requests without range or dates reads every retained day. The paged views return 10 rows by default (up to 100) with a top-level next_cursor; changing a filter needs a new first page, while a continuation may change limit. Failed-verification requests are left out unless verification asks for them. unavailable not_connected means no crawl-log source is connected and no logs are retained for the window; connection awaiting_data or missing coverage means unknown, not zero. Use read_ai_crawlability for robots permission and read_ai_traffic_pages for activity per page.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

view.description: summary is totals; crawlers is one row per AI crawler; coverage is how complete each day of logs is; requests lists individual requests, paged.

range.description: A preset window ending today; or pass start_date and end_date instead.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

verification.description: Keep only crawler requests whose claimed identity was verified, could not be verified, or failed verification.

bot_id.description: A bot_id the crawlers view returned; keep only that crawler.

status.description: An HTTP status code; keep only requests answered with it.

folder.description: A site path prefix such as /blog/ to read only pages under it.

resource_class.description: A resource_class a previous row returned, such as page, to read only that kind.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_demand
tools.title: Read search demand
tools.description: Read the latest search-demand snapshot: the opportunities CiteLadder found in the project's own Search Console data for one window, such as queries in striking distance of page one, pages competing for the same query, click-through below the site's norm and rising or falling queries. It returns the window (pass it to read_query_evidence for the query rows behind it), the signal count by type, each detector's state, coverage (whether search data and query evidence were observed) and the change in signal count against the previous snapshot, which is not a cause. unavailable no_demand_snapshot means no snapshot was built yet, usually because Search Console is not connected or still importing; read_integration_status says which. The signals become Actions: use read_actions for the prioritized work. Keyword volumes from research live in read_search_intelligence.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

tools.name: read_fact_checks
tools.title: Read fact checks
tools.description: Read whether AI answers state the brand's facts correctly. Factual claims answers made about the brand in the latest or a chosen run are checked against the brand's confirmed facts. The summary view gives accuracy (supported out of supported plus contradicted) with its coverage, by topic and engine, the contradicted claims with the fact they contradict, and sources cited alongside them. The claims view lists every checked claim with its quote, verdict and the facts used, paged (50 by default, pass next_cursor); edited true means a person replaced the model's verdict, so report the person's. The facts view lists each confirmed fact with how many claims supported or contradicted it (counts kind not_raised or pending means no claim to count yet, never zero), to find the facts answers get wrong most. Use read_perception for tone rather than accuracy. Always state the coverage and quote the fact. accuracy_state not_enabled, no_facts, no_claims, pending or unavailable means there is no value, never zero; inconclusive and not_covered are not errors in the answer. Sources are cited alongside a contradiction, never its cause.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

view.description: summary is accuracy and its coverage; claims lists the checked claims, paged; facts lists each fact with its verdict counts.

topic.description: With view claims: keep only claims about this kind of fact.

verdict.description: With view claims: keep only this verdict; contradicted finds the errors.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_integration_status
tools.title: Read connected data
tools.description: Read which data sources (Search Console, GA4, server logs) are connected to the project and how far their import has got, to explain why a traffic or search read is unavailable. It returns the overall stage (not_connected, connected, importing, core_data_ready, analysis_ready or import_failed), the backfill state and the date data is imported through, whether performance and demand snapshots exist, and each connection with its provider, property and last sync. Read it when another read returns unavailable or not_connected, before reading that again. Connecting a source happens in CiteLadder, not through this tool.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

tools.name: read_page_text
tools.title: Read page text
tools.description: Read the words of one crawled page of the project's site, by URL or by site_url_id from read_site_pages: its title, meta description, h1-h3 headings, then the visible body text (up to 36000 characters in all; text_chars_omitted counts any body text left out), with its URL, page type and when it was fetched. Use it to quote, review or rewrite what a page actually says. It reads the latest crawl, or crawl_id; it never fetches the live page, so the copy is as of fetched_at. unavailable page_not_crawled means the crawl has no page at that address, and crawled_urls lists the nearest crawled addresses to try; no_site_crawl means no crawl exists.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

crawl_id.description: A crawl id that read_site_health returned; omit for the latest crawl.

url.description: The page address, such as https://example.com/pricing; scheme, www and a trailing slash are ignored.

site_url_id.description: A page id (site_url_id) from read_site_pages; pass this or url.

tools.name: read_perception
tools.title: Read answer perception
tools.description: Read how AI answers portray the brand and competitors in the latest or a chosen run: net sentiment (-100 to +100) per brand, engine, topic and prompt, each with its coverage; praise and criticism by theme; per brand, competitors included, how many classified mentions raised each theme (theme_mentions, counts only: quotes are the brand's own); how often answers recommend or advise against the brand; and the sources cited alongside criticism. The summary view returns all of that; the quotes view lists the verified quotes behind it, paged (50 by default, pass next_cursor). The response is always available: read perception_state, where pending, unavailable or no_mentions means there is no value, never zero. Always state the coverage. Sources are cited alongside criticism, never its cause. Use read_fact_checks for whether answers are factually right, and read_visibility_overview for how often the brand is mentioned at all. view probe is the market probe: its latest launch, schedule and how engines describe the category; view objections lists the probe's objection groups with their ids, paged.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

view.description: summary is sentiment and themes per brand; quotes lists the verified quotes, paged; probe and objections read the market probe.

entity.description: With view quotes: a brand exactly as the summary names it, to quote only it.

theme.description: With view quotes: keep only quotes about this theme, as the summary names it.

polarity.description: With view quotes: keep only praise or only criticism.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_performance
tools.title: Read search performance
tools.description: Read the site's organic search performance from Search Console and GA4: clicks, impressions, CTR, average position, sessions and key events for a window, with a series over time and an optional comparison window. Without dimension it returns totals, the series, data coverage and how many rows each breakdown has; with dimension it returns one page of rows by query, page, country, device or day (10 by default, pass next_cursor for more). The range defaults to last_synced, all imported data; most custom windows have no saved snapshot and return performance_range_not_projected, so prefer the preset ranges. not_connected means no search source is connected, which is not zero; read_integration_status says why. Use read_query_evidence for queries matched to crawled pages, and read_ai_referrals for traffic from AI assistants.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

granularity.description: The bucket size of the totals over time.

compare.description: The window to compare against; custom needs the compare dates.

compare_start_date.description: First day of a custom comparison window, inclusive.

compare_end_date.description: Last day of a custom comparison window, inclusive.

dimension.description: Break the totals down by this dimension, paged.

sort.description: With dimension: one of clicks, ctr, dimension_key, impressions, position; prefix - for descending, such as -clicks.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: With dimension: rows per page.

tools.name: read_prompt_metrics
tools.title: Read prompt metrics
tools.description: Find which prompts the brand wins or loses. view list ranks one run's prompts by score, each with its visibility and citation rates, share of voice, average position, win rate, net sentiment, web search share, the brands its answers named and its change against the previous run, paged (pass next_cursor). view history is one prompt's score per run with the Actions implemented along the way; view answers lists that prompt's answers across runs, newest first, with the brands named, your position, whether you were cited and whether the engine searched, each with a citeladder:// id for fetch. Null rates, win rate or sentiment are unavailable or not applicable, never zero. list defaults to the latest completed run; unavailable no_completed_run means none has finished. Use read_prompt_portfolio for the wording and topic of every tracked prompt, and read_visibility_results for every answer of one run.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

view.description: list is one run's prompts (the default); history and answers are one prompt across runs and need prompt_id.

prompt_id.description: A prompt id from read_prompt_portfolio or read_prompt_metrics.

audit_id.description: With view list: a run id (audit_id); omit for the latest.

baseline_id.description: With view list: an earlier run id to measure change against.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_prompt_portfolio
tools.title: Read prompts
tools.description: List the prompts the project tracks, so you know what is measured before reading results or changing prompts. Each row has the prompt id, text, topic, intent, buyer stage, cohort (core prompts are scored; comparison prompts name a competitor and are reported separately), status and whether audits measure it now, plus its prompt set and topic_id. topics lists every project topic (id, name, description), including topics with no prompts yet; topics_truncated says the list is partial. Rows come oldest first, in pages; pass next_cursor for more. To find one prompt by its wording use search; to see what engines answered for a prompt use read_visibility_results with its prompt_id. view sets lists every prompt set, empty ones included; view candidates lists suggested prompts waiting for review, with their ids.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

prompt_set_id.description: A prompt set id from an earlier row of this tool; omit for every set in the project.

view.description: prompts (the default), sets or candidates; each is paged.

cohort.description: Keep only scored or only comparison prompts; combines with the other filters.

intent.description: Keep only prompts with this intent; evaluation marks brand prompts.

active_only.description: true keeps only prompts audits measure now; false (the default) also lists disabled and archived ones.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_query_evidence
tools.title: Read queries by page
tools.description: Read the Search Console queries that bring searchers to each site page, matched to pages CiteLadder crawled, for one saved window. Use it to see which queries a page ranks for, or which page answers a query; for totals and trends use read_performance, and for the search signals found in the same window use read_demand. The window must exactly match a saved one: read_demand returns it. Any other window returns unavailable exact_query_evidence_window_not_projected, which is not zero. Each row is one query and page with its totals over the whole window, largest impressions first: the query, the page Search Console reported, the crawled page it was matched to (site_url_id), how the match was made (resolution_outcome), impressions, clicks, CTR (clicks divided by impressions), the impression-weighted average position and the number of days with data. Pass site_url_id to read every query of one page in a call or two. granularity day returns the daily rows behind the totals instead, each with a citeladder:// id for fetch. Rows come in pages; pass next_cursor for more, with the same granularity and filters. Country, device and search type are not broken out.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

window_start.description: First day of a saved window, inclusive: read_demand's window.start.

window_end.description: Last day of the same saved window, inclusive: read_demand's window.end.

query.description: One search query, matched exactly ignoring case and spacing, not a search.

site_url_id.description: A page id (site_url_id) from read_site_pages or an earlier row; keep only its queries.

resolution_outcome.description: Keep only queries whose page match was exact, resolved (for example through a redirect or canonical), ambiguous or unresolved. All filters combine.

granularity.description: window (the default) totals each query and page over the window; day lists the daily rows.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_query_fanouts
tools.title: Read query fanouts
tools.description: Read the web searches engines ran while answering one run's prompts: each query with how often it ran, its share of every search, its change against the previous comparable run (null when not compared), the engines and prompts behind it, how many of its answers named the brand, and the tracked brands the query itself names (null when the run counted no queries). event_count, distinct_queries and coverage describe the whole run, unaffected by paging. order top ranks by share; rising and falling by change. Pass search to match query text, prompt_id or topic_id to narrow. It defaults to the latest completed run; unavailable no_completed_run means none has finished. Use read_prompt_metrics for the prompts themselves.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

topic_id.description: A topic id from read_prompt_portfolio; keep only answers to prompts filed under it when their run was measured. unavailable topic_not_measured means the run asked no prompt in it.

prompt_id.description: A prompt id from read_prompt_portfolio or read_prompt_metrics.

order.description: top by share (the default); rising or falling by change since the last run.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_search_dataset
tools.title: Read a research dataset
tools.description: Read the rows of one saved keyword or backlink research dataset, after read_search_intelligence has named it. Use it for keyword volumes, rankings, competitor keywords or referring domains; use read_search_intelligence to choose the dataset and read_query_evidence for the project's own Search Console queries. It returns the dataset (kind, target, market, saved row count) and a page of rows (50 by default; pass next_cursor for more, with the same sort), each with a citeladder:// id for fetch. Columns depend on the dataset kind. Referring-domain and page totals are provider aggregates, not individual links: never report them as a link list. Rows are as saved at research time and are never refreshed by this read.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

dataset_id.description: A dataset id from read_search_intelligence; a dataset of another project is refused.

sort.description: The column to order by, which must exist for the dataset kind: one of backlinks, dataforseo_rank, difficulty, domain, etv, id, intent, keyword, owned_rank_group, rank_group, referring_main_domains, search_volume, url, backlinks_spam_score, broken_backlinks, broken_pages, cpc, organic_keywords, rank_absolute, referring_domains, referring_pages. Omit to order by row id. Rows with no value sort last.

direction.description: asc (the default) or desc; desc with a volume or rank column puts the largest first.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_search_intelligence
tools.title: Read keyword and backlink research
tools.description: List the keyword, competitor and backlink research datasets saved for this project, and whether the research provider is connected. Each dataset has its id, kind, target domain, market (location and language), status and whether its totals are aggregates rather than individual links, plus the project's owned targets, tracked competitors and latest research run. Pass a dataset id to read_search_dataset for its rows. unavailable with no datasets means no research was run yet; this tool never starts research, which happens in CiteLadder. For the project's own Search Console queries use read_query_evidence instead. view runs lists research runs with status, newest first, including runs awaiting confirmation.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_seed_queries
tools.title: Read seed queries
tools.description: List the searches a prompt generation run could ground its wording on, for each search data source the project has (search_console or search_intelligence): each query's id, text and topic. Only non-branded, question-like searches are listed; a seed steers wording and is never copied into a prompt. There is no volume or impression count: never present a query as AI prompt volume. unavailable no_search_data means no source is connected.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

tools.name: read_site_health
tools.title: Read Site Health
tools.description: Read the Site Health summary of the latest crawl, or a chosen snapshot: the web fundamentals and AI-readiness scores with their measurement state, how many pages were selected and analyzed, and the top 10 issues, each with its rule_id, severity, description, remediation and how many pages it affects. unavailable no_site_snapshot means no crawl was analyzed yet; this tool never starts one. view changes summarizes what changed between the last two crawls and change_list lists each change; aeo_readiness breaks the AI-readiness score down per dimension and check; architecture is page types, depth, orphans and the page tree. Use read_site_pages with a rule_id to list the affected pages and read_ai_crawlability for robots access. Use render_site_health to show the user the interactive view. view issues lists every issue group of the crawl with its group_id, paged; view schedule is the recurring crawl.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

snapshot_id.description: A Site Health snapshot id, or the crawl id it was built from; omit for the latest crawl.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_site_links
tools.title: Read internal links
tools.description: Read the internal links of crawled pages: per page, inbound and outbound link counts (overall and in main content) and nofollow inbound links, click depth from the home page, a bounded sample of the pages linking to it and linked from it with their anchors, and anchor diagnostics. Use it to find orphaned or buried pages. Pass up to 10 site_url_ids from read_site_pages to read those pages in one call (with smaller neighbor samples and anchor diagnostics counted by kind); missing_site_url_ids lists any without link metrics in this crawl (for example a page that was not analyzed). Otherwise rows come in pages; pass next_cursor for more. unavailable no_site_crawl means no crawl exists. Use read_site_pages for page scores and issues. view analyses gives the internal-link analyses with their ids and state, latest first.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

crawl_id.description: A crawl id that read_site_health returned; omit for the latest crawl.

site_url_ids.description: Page ids (site_url_id) from read_site_pages; omit to page through every page.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_site_pages
tools.title: Read site pages
tools.description: Pages from a crawl, paged: URL, title, page type, status, scores, issue count and the rule ids of each page's issues by finding class. Pass url to find a page by its address, rule_id (from read_site_health top_issues or an issue group) to list exactly the pages affected by that issue, each with rule_evidence: what that check found on that page (a site-level architecture issue is recorded once on the home page, and its rule_evidence names the affected pages), and, when the crawl kept one, a reference_snippet: redacted markup of the failing element and its label context from one affected page (text and attribute values replaced by [text] and [redacted]), to write an exact fix; filter by page_kind or status to find pages by type or status. This returns metadata, not page copy: use read_page_text for a page's words. view issue_history with site_url_id lists the issues that page has resolved. read_site_health gives the totals.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

crawl_id.description: A crawl id that read_site_health returned; omit for the latest crawl.

url.description: A page address or part of one, such as https://example.com/pricing or /pricing; keeps pages whose URL contains it, ignoring scheme, www and a trailing slash.

rule_id.description: A Site Health rule_id; returns only the pages with a current issue of it.

page_kind.description: Keep only pages of this type.

status.description: Keep only pages in this state.

site_url_id.description: With view issue_history: a page id from this tool.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_source_url
tools.title: Read a cited page
tools.description: Read one cited page in depth, after read_visibility_sources or an answer names it: how often it was retrieved and cited, when first and last seen, the engines and models that cite it, the prompts it is cited for (up to 50), the brands it names (up to 12, including whether yours is there), and what CiteLadder read on the page itself. Omit audit_id to cover every run in the market, not just the latest. The URL must match the cited URL exactly; unavailable url_not_cited_in_selection means it was not cited in that selection.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

url.description: A cited URL exactly as read_visibility_sources or an answer listed it.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for every run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

tools.name: read_visibility_overview
tools.title: Read AI visibility
tools.description: Read the headline AI visibility of one run: how often answers mention the brand and cite its site, the visibility score, rankings of the brand against each competitor (mention rate, citation rate, share of voice, average position among the brands an answer named, win rate and net sentiment), a breakdown per engine with its win rate, and the run's status and answer counts. Win rate is how often a brand was named first among the answers naming any tracked brand; null win_rate or sentiment means unavailable or not applicable, never zero, and sentiment always comes with its classified count. It defaults to the latest completed run in the default market; pass baseline_id to compare two runs. view topics returns visibility, share of voice, position, rank and win rate per project topic; view matrix pairs engines, topics, markets and brands from each market's latest run, where not_run cells are unmeasured, never zero. view surface is AI Overview rates per search engine (trigger, brand and owned citation, each with its denominator); view markets is every market's latest headline. Pass topic_id to read one topic. Each market is measured separately: pass market_id for another market, and never pool markets. unavailable no_completed_run means no run has finished yet; metrics_pending means the latest run has finished but its results are still being written, so try again later rather than report that nothing was measured; topic_not_measured means the run asked no prompt in that topic. Use read_visibility_trends for change over time, read_prompt_metrics for which prompts are won or lost, read_competitors for one competitor in depth, read_visibility_results for the answers themselves, and read_visibility_sources for what was cited. view runs lists every audit with status and progress, newest first; view run with audit_id adds its failed answers; view schedules lists audit schedules with their ids.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

baseline_id.description: With view summary: an earlier run id (audit_id) to compare against.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

topic_id.description: A topic id from read_prompt_portfolio; keep only answers to prompts filed under it when their run was measured. unavailable topic_not_measured means the run asked no prompt in it.

view.description: summary is the run (the default); topics is one row per topic; matrix is the engine, topic, market and brand grids; surface is Google AI Overview and AI Mode rates; markets lists every market; runs, run and schedules are paged.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_visibility_results
tools.title: Read AI answers
tools.description: Read the answers engines gave in one run, to see exactly what an engine said for a prompt. Each answer has the prompt text, engine, model, repetition, whether web search was used, the brands mentioned (with first position) and every citation (URL, domain, whether it is your site or a competitor's), plus a citeladder:// id for fetch. It defaults to the latest completed run in the default market; unavailable no_completed_run means none has finished. Answers come in pages; pass next_cursor for more. Only core prompts are included unless cohort is comparison or all. Filters (prompt_id, topic_id, domain, url, engine) combine. For one prompt's answers across every run use read_prompt_metrics view answers. Use read_visibility_overview for rates and read_visibility_sources for citation totals.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

topic_id.description: A topic id from read_prompt_portfolio; keep only answers to prompts filed under it when their run was measured. unavailable topic_not_measured means the run asked no prompt in it.

prompt_id.description: A prompt id from read_prompt_portfolio; keep only its answers.

domain.description: A domain such as example.com; keep only rows citing it.

url.description: Keep only answers that cite this exact URL.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_visibility_sources
tools.title: Read cited sources
tools.description: Rank the domains or pages AI answers cited in one run, to find the sources worth earning a place on. Each row has how many answers and prompts cited it, its citation share and rate, ownership (yours, a competitor's or third party) and category; page rows also list up to 3 brands named on the page and whether there is an Action for it. It defaults to the latest run; unavailable no_completed_run means none has finished. Rows come in pages; pass next_cursor for more. level domain lists publishers; level url, or passing domain, lists pages. Pass topic_id for the sources of one topic's answers. view near_misses lists your pages engines read but did not cite; movers, the sources whose citation share rose or fell against the comparable earlier run; series, citation share over time across runs (pass domain for one source). Use read_source_url for one page in depth, and read_visibility_results for the answers that cite it.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

topic_id.description: A topic id from read_prompt_portfolio; keep only answers to prompts filed under it when their run was measured. unavailable topic_not_measured means the run asked no prompt in it.

level.description: domain counts publishers (the default); url counts individual pages.

domain.description: A cited domain such as example.com; with level url, lists its pages.

granularity.description: With view series: the length of each point.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_visibility_trends
tools.title: Read visibility trends
tools.description: Read how visibility changed over an explicit window of at most 366 days, as points per run or per day, week or month. Each point has the visibility score, brand mention and citation rates, share of voice, average position, rankings of every brand (with position and win rate), the model and whether web search was on, a comparison_key and events: what changed at that point (prompt_panel: prompts added, archived or removed; model_change: an engine's model changed; action_live: an Action went live). Points with different comparison keys were measured differently and are not comparable; name the events when you explain a change, and compare like with like. Gaps are missing runs, not zero. At most the newest 100 points are returned. Pass topic_id to follow one topic. unavailable no_measured_runs means no run fell in the window. Use read_visibility_overview for one run in depth, or with baseline_id to compare exactly two runs.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

topic_id.description: A topic id from read_prompt_portfolio; keep only answers to prompts filed under it when their run was measured. unavailable topic_not_measured means the run asked no prompt in it.

from_at.description: Start of the window, with a UTC offset, such as 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z.

to_at.description: End of the window, after from_at and at most 366 days later.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

granularity.description: One point per run (the default), or per day, week or month.

transport_model.description: Keep only runs answered by this model, as a previous point named it.

retrieval_enabled.description: true keeps only runs with web search on; false only runs without it.

tools.name: render_site_health
tools.title: Show Site Health
tools.description: Show the user an interactive Site Health view (scores, coverage and top issues) for the latest or a chosen snapshot, in clients that display apps. To reason over the data yourself, use read_site_health.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

snapshot_id.description: A Site Health snapshot id, or the crawl id it was built from; omit for the latest crawl.

tools.name: render_visibility
tools.title: Show AI visibility
tools.description: Show the user an interactive visibility view, in clients that display apps: overview, trends over a window, or cited sources for one run. To reason over the numbers yourself, use read_visibility_overview, read_visibility_trends or read_visibility_sources.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

view.description: Which view to show; each other field says the views it applies to.

audit_id.description: Overview or sources: a run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

snapshot_id.description: Site Health only: a snapshot id; omit for the latest crawl.

engine.description: Show one engine only, such as chatgpt; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is reported separately.

from_at.description: Trends only, required there: start of the window.

to_at.description: Trends only, required there: end of the window.

transport_model.description: Trends only: keep only runs answered by this model.

retrieval_enabled.description: Trends only: true keeps runs with web search on, false runs without it.

competitor.description: Overview or trends: a competitor exactly as the rankings name it, to highlight.

level.description: Sources only: domain lists publishers (the default); url lists pages.

domain.description: Sources only: a cited domain such as example.com, to list its pages.

cursor.description: Sources only: the next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: Sources only: rows per page.

tools.name: search
tools.title: Search
tools.description: Find projects, Actions (every status, open and in-progress first; each result states its status) and prompts by text when you do not know where a record is. Returns matching records with ids; pass one to fetch for the full record.

query.description: Words to look for, such as a prompt or brand.

project_id.description: Search one project only; omit to search every project.

limit.description: How many matches to return.
